text:
ashley: Quick heads-up — opened a docs PR to relax the function-calling output guardrails so we can handle partial/nullable tool outputs more gracefully. See PR: https://git.redwood/infer/docs/pull/842

ashley: TL;DR: we introduce a permissive envelope `result` where the `payload` can be null and consumers should use a provided `parseRelaxed()` helper in SDKs. This should reduce spurts of broken examples when models emit small mistakes.

mike: nice. can you paste the example diff?

ashley: sure — snippet from the PR:```json
- {"tool": "lookup_price", "output": {"price": 12.34}}
+ {"tool": "lookup_price", "result": {"payload": {"price": 12.34}, "confidence": 0.92} }
+ // or when partial/failed
+ {"tool": "lookup_price", "result": null }
```

priya: couple questions: 1) does `result: null` mean we should keep the old parse code path? 2) how do we indicate transient failures vs legit null results?

ashley: good q. we added an optional `reason` string inside `result` for failures, but it’s optional so legacy outputs still parse. schema excerpt:```json
"result": {
  "oneOf": [
    { "type": "null" },
    { "type": "object", "properties": { "payload": {}, "confidence": {"type": "number"}, "reason": {"type": "string"} } }
  ]
}
```

mike: sounds backwards-compatible. i’m worried examples across the docs site will break (we have literal example outputs used by the parser tests). any migration plan? :eyes:

jordan: i can run a quick grep + script to patch snippet outputs and add `// tolerant parse` comments. will follow-up with a PR to the examples repo.

priya: SDK updates: i’ll add `parseRelaxed()` to the TS SDK that first tries strict JSON, then runs a small pre-clean (trim trailing commas, wrap bare `true`/`null` into envelope) and finally falls back to JSON5. patch will be small. snippet:```ts
// old
const out = JSON.parse(resp.text);
// new
const out = parseRelaxed(resp.text);
```

ashley: perfect. can you also add a short migration note in the docs site under "structured outputs" explaining `result: null` semantics + `reason` field? a single paragraph is fine.

jordan: yep. i’ll also add redirect docs for old links that reference `output` field to point to `result` via a small client-side rewrite. planning to run link-finder first.

doc_bot: NOTE: docs CI failed on the examples site (link-check) after the PR — 12 broken links found. https://ci.redwood/infer/1234

mike: can someone paste one broken example so i can triage?

ashley: example: `examples/funcall/README.md` shows `"output"` top-level. need replace with `"result.payload"` or note nullability.

priya: i’ll handle the SDK patch + unit tests. mike — can you run the examples smoke after jordan’s snippet patch?

mike: yep, i’ll run smoke on my laptop and on CI once jordan pushes the example PR.

ashley: thanks all. timeline: aim to merge schema + SDK helpers today, follow-up example patches tomorrow. @jordan please tag me when examples PR is up so i can quick review. :thumbsup:

jordan: will do. starting the grep now, ping if you see weird diffs. /cc @doc_bot for CI watch

doc_bot: Deployment note: docs site rebuild queued. ETA ~12m. Will post results.

ashley: if CI passes and the SDK tests are green, i’ll ship the migration note and close PR 842.

mike: small nit — can we add a one-liner in the console docs showing the `parseRelaxed()` shim? it’ll cut down support questions.

priya: adding it to the SDK README now. i’ll include the exact code sample and mention edgecases (unclosed arrays, trailing commas, enum vs string mismatches).

ashley: awesome. thanks team.
